A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SOKE and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Renumbered supplementary content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original multilingual generation experiments, ablations, pose-reconstruction evaluations, and a study with professional ASL and CSL signers.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds unaligned joint-error measurements and monolingual generation results.

M1.justification: The decoupled tokenizer, multi-head decoding, retrieval procedure, training losses, and greedy inference remain unchanged. The dictionary-source wording does not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: The three generation benchmarks, languages, and SGNify evaluation remain unchanged. However, Section 3.4 replaces v2's explicit dictionary assignments, including SLR500, with broader dataset citations and unspecified online sources. The PDFs do not establish whether dictionary training or retrieval coverage actually changed.

E2.justification: The main benchmark and pose-fitting comparator sets are unchanged. Table S8 adds S-MotionGPT to the monolingual-training analysis, reusing its earlier scores; v2's scalability analysis in Table 3 compared only SOKE training configurations.

E3.justification: Section 4 now distinguishes Procrustes-aligned from original joint errors, relabeling retained scores and adding unaligned evaluation. Table S8 adds CSL-only and Phoenix-only training controls beyond the existing How2Sign-only setting. These changes do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table S8 extends the training-data analysis to examine whether SOKE's advantage persists under monolingual training on each benchmark. The existing decoding, retrieval, tokenizer, codebook-size, and embedding-weight analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 7 retains identical user-study ratings and error bars. Neither version adds seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or explanations of the error bars.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds unaligned errors, including SOKE's How2Sign body/hand values of 7.75/10.08. Table S8 adds monolingual CSL and Phoenix averages of 4.18 and 3.83. Some baseline average-error entries disappear. Existing component scores and BLEU-4 results remain unchanged; Section 4.1 switches highlighted averages to previously reported hand errors, rather than showing performance gains.

T1.justification: The quantization, decoding factorizations, conditional-independence assumption, and loss formulations are unchanged. Appendix equations S1–S3 become S5–S7 without mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unified multilingual generation, efficient multi-head decoding, retrieval guidance, curated poses, and state-of-the-art performance on three benchmarks.

C2.justification: Explanations involving embedding fusion, retrieval guidance, and cross-lingual sharing remain unchanged, as do the pose-reconstruction limitations and future-work discussion. The new monolingual paragraph reports comparative findings without adding a substantive mechanism explanation or limitation.

D1.justification: v3 makes dictionary provenance less explicit, removes the promised public release of code/models/data and the mBART checkpoint link, and directs video access to the project page instead of an enclosed MP4. Hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain unchanged. These edits do not establish actual resource withdrawal.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including SignLLM, Uni-Sign, SignBERT+, and Sign-IDD, while removing the SLR500 source citation and the general DTW reference. These update the supporting literature without substantially changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to the author line, abstract ending, dictionary and metric descriptions, acknowledgments, and a short monolingual-results paragraph. The section order and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains separate aligned/unaligned metric groups and loses average columns; Table 2's metric headings change, and Table S8 is added. Existing illustrations and the user-study chart are retained, with supplementary renumbering and limited layout shifts.

improvement.justification: Distinguishing aligned and unaligned errors in Table 1 and adding monolingual controls in Table S8 modestly strengthen the evaluation and support advantages beyond multilingual training. The gain is limited because v2 already included a How2Sign-only ablation, and less explicit dictionary provenance partly offsets the improved evidence.
